blocks.summary: The paper motivates visual token dilution in long multimodal reasoning and proposes training-free visual token coreset reinjection.
VisRef is positioned between costly training-based look-back methods and text-centric test-time scaling.
Related work covers MLRMs, test-time scaling, visual refocusing, and tool-using multimodal agents.
The paper formalizes standard thinking, textual self-reflection, and visual-integrated trajectories.
DPP-based coreset selection uses a text-conditioned kernel and a log-determinant relevance-diversity decomposition.
Experiments evaluate MathVista, MathVision, and MM-Star on InternVL3.5-8B, Qwen-3-VL-8B, and SAIL-VL2-8B.
Discussion validates relevance-diversity balance, entropy threshold, token budget, and attention focusing.
Conclusion restates selective DPP visual reinjection and entropy stopping as a training-free visual grounding route.
Appendix reports limitations, implementation settings, additional benchmarks, latency, model scaling, and extra ablations.
